title: State Composition
description: Compose local and remote state in Apollo Client for unified data management.

data.text: Real applications need both server state and client state. Apollo Client shines when you compose these together: server data lives in the normalized cache, client UI state lives in reactive variables or local-only fields, and both can be queried together.

data.title: Composed query
data.content: Combining server and local state in one component.

data.text: Avoid duplicating server data in local state. If the server already provides a value, read it from the cache. Local state should only store data that the server cannot or should not provide.
data.title: Single Source of Truth
State Composition Key Points
points: Server and client state can coexist in Apollo.
Query both remote and local fields together.
Use the right tool for each state type.
data.takeaway: Composing local and remote state in Apollo Client simplifies data management and reduces prop drilling.
